clue.text: Sadly slightly altered church in French region

indicators.note: a word only slightly altered keeps its letters but has a couple swapped around

parts.note: an exclamation of regret, meaning sadly
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone notes with regret that a church in a French region has been changed a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle two letters of ALAS swap places, which is why the setter says it is only slightly altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is the north-eastern province of France bordering Germany, so it is a French region.

clue.text: Golfing expert interrupting a chap playing golf shot

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
playing suggests the letters are being toyed with and set in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder
a pro is a professional, as at a golf club

explanation.surface: A golf professional cuts in on a fellow who is in the middle of playing a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters become AP-ACH and the professional sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an approach is the stroke played towards the green from the fairway.

clue.text: Summary is amount of money raised on board

indicators.note: in a down entry something raised is read from the bottom upwards, so it runs backwards
being on board means being inside a ship, here the abbreviation for steamship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel being boarded
a pony is slang for twenty-five pounds
taken as written

explanation.surface: A précis notes the sum collected aboard ship for a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds. The word 'is', though first in the clue, goes at the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synopsis is a brief outline giving the main points, which is what a summary is.

clue.text: Fish produced by a cricket club I love as starter

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
taken as written
standard abbreviation for cricket club
taken as written
love is a zero score in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A cricket club diner says the fish dish was their favourite first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like the definition alongside 'starter', but it only supplies the opening letters; the definition is the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpaccio is an Italian appetiser of very thin slices of raw beef or fish, served as a first course.

clue.text: Large flat, not grand, requiring renovation nevertheless

indicators.note: a place needing renovation must be rebuilt, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order
not having something means it is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: the letters of both words are the starting material
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An estate agent admits a big apartment, though not posh, still needs doing up.
explanation.definitionFit: After all and nevertheless are both adverbial phrases meaning in spite of what has been said.

clue.text: Fellow with youngster also appearing in excellent quiz show

indicators.note: things appearing in something else are placed inside it

parts.note: first part of FINE, meaning excellent
F is the abbreviation for fellow
a teen is a young person
too means also
end of FINE, meaning excellent

explanation.surface: A man and a youngster both turn up on a first-rate television quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifteen to One is a long-running British TV quiz in which fifteen contestants are whittled down to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifteen to One is the title of a Channel 4 television quiz programme, so it is an example of a quiz show.

clue.text: Support for artist in rental agreement, first to last

indicators.note: sending the first letter to the end shifts the whole word round by one place

parts.note: a lease is a contract for renting property

explanation.surface: An artist's rental contract includes some support, as a clause might.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the wooden frame that holds up an artist's canvas while painting.

clue.text: Wading bird one's first caught clutched by a doctor

indicators.note: something clutched is held inside another's grip

parts.note: A plus VET, the animal doctor, opening part

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: opening letter of one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
rest of A VET, a vet being an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A vet holds a captured wading bird that came first in something.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wader with an upturned bill, so it is a wading bird.

clue.text: Repetitive series in metropolitan yearbook

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A city almanac lists the same items over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long tedious recital or list, originally a repeated series of prayers.

clue.text: Writer with anger banishing initial privation

indicators.note: banishing the initial sends away the opening letter

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
fury is great anger

explanation.surface: An angry author tries to drive out the hardship of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Penury is extreme poverty, a synonym of privation, the lack of basic necessities.

clue.text: Branch cancelled filming work

parts.note: an event that is off has been cancelled
a shoot is a session of filming

explanation.surface: A local office reports that its film production has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch' reads as an office of a company, but the definition is the botanical or figurative side shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side growth from a plant or an organisation that has split off, just as a branch is.

clue.text: Presenter of 5, broadcasting king (TV said so)

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: every letter of these words is the fodder

explanation.surface: Television reports a monarch's announcement, apparently on the authority of the TV itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandi Toksvig, the Danish-born British comedian and broadcaster, hosted Fifteen to One (5-down) from 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the host of the revived Channel 4 quiz, the answer to 5-down, so she presented it.

clue.text: Place in which issue is raised without natural authority?

definitions.text: Place in which issue is raised without natural authority?

parts.words: Place in which issue is raised without natural authority?
parts.note: surface reading: a forum where a matter is brought up without any proper power behind it

parts.words: issue is raised without natural authority
parts.note: setter's reading: issue means offspring, raised means brought up, and natural authority means birth parents

explanation.surface: A meeting where a question gets aired though nobody has real authority to settle it.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue is a legal word for children, so the clue describes a home where children grow up without their parents.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is an institution caring for children whose parents have died, so they are brought up without them.

clue.text: An extension to being out?

parts.note: surface reading: extra time added to a period away from home or a spell out of play
setter's reading: being out cold, asleep, and the extension is staying asleep in bed longer

explanation.surface: A request for extra time out of the office or away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Out here means unconscious or sound asleep, so extending it is sleeping late.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a morning spent staying in bed later than usual, prolonging sleep.

clue.text: Police in bit surprisingly net gangster by chance

definitions.note: adverbial phrase defining an adjective; read as 'happening by chance'

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: a bit is a small coin
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department
these letters are rearranged
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Detectives involved in a sting happen to catch a mobster in their trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but here the police simply go in after the bit, placed alongside rather than inside. A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coincidental happens by chance, by a fortuitous coinciding of events.

clue.text: Gradual decrease in hands?

parts.note: surface reading: a slow loss of strength or size in someone's hands
setter's reading: hands are workers, so this is a workforce shrinking as staff leave and are not replaced

explanation.surface: Someone notices their hands slowly getting smaller or weaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Attrition is the reduction of a workforce through natural wastage, with leavers not being replaced.

clue.text: Crooked fool curtailed police operation

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a twit is a fool
a sting is an undercover police operation to trap criminals

explanation.surface: A dishonest idiot cuts short an undercover police operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' sounds like dishonest, fitting the police, but the definition means bent out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisting can mean contorted or bending, so something twisting is crooked rather than straight.

clue.text: Uniformed schoolboy obviously getting on with former Yugoslav right away

parts.note: grey hair is a visible sign of ageing

indicators.note: with right sent away, the letter standing for right is removed

parts.note: Croatia was part of the former Yugoslavia
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A uniformed pupil plainly gets along well with a Croatian classmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' reads as getting along with someone, but here it means growing old. Grey-coat schools were charity schools, such as Grey Coat Hospital in Westminster, whose pupils wore grey uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey-coat was a pupil of a charity school whose uniform was a grey coat.

clue.text: Direct in leftward direction queen in airport building

parts.note: to direct is to control
to W, towards the west, which is left on a map
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer the queen leftwards inside an airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Maps put west on the left, so heading leftward is going TO W.
explanation.definitionFit: The control tower is the building at an airfield from which air traffic is directed.

clue.text: A second trip on water in storm

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
a sail is a voyage in a boat

explanation.surface: A further boat outing caught up in rough weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' sits at the end like a noun for bad weather, but it is a verb meaning to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, as an army does when it storms a position.

clue.text: Criminal type making small quantity in effect?

indicators.note: putting one thing in another is, in effect, what builds the answer here

parts.note: a bit is a small amount
the ampersand is a piece of printer's type standing for and

explanation.surface: A crook is the sort of person who makes a small amount effectively count.
explanation.walkthrough: Type means the printed character &, read as AND, which goes into BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber, especially one of an armed gang, so a criminal.

clue.text: Crew in five lines?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the people employed in an organisation
second meaning: the set of five horizontal lines on which music is written

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a team lined up in five rows; the musical sense of the word is the five lines themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff means a body of workers, and in music it is another name for the stave of five lines.

clue.text: Religious ruling defended by chief at Walsingham

indicators.note: something defended is surrounded and guarded, so the answer is held within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A church edict is upheld by the head of the shrine at Walsingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Walsingham is a Norfolk village famous as a Christian pilgrimage shrine, which makes the Islamic ruling a neat surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a legal ruling on a point of Islamic law given by a recognised authority.

clue.text: Artist showing English footballer, short and dainty, grabbing last of goals

indicators.note: to grab something is to take hold of it, so one piece goes inside the other
something short is missing its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Harry Kane, the England striker
first part of DINKY, meaning dainty

indicators.note: the last of a word is only its final letter

parts.note: final letter of goals
end of DINKY

explanation.walkthrough: Dinky is British for small and neat. KANE loses its end and DINKY takes in the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassily Kandinsky was the Russian painter credited as a pioneer of abstract art.

clue.text: Supplement mentioned by Frenchman in a seedy joint

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits within it

parts.note: A plus DIVE, a seedy bar, opening part
dit is French for said or mentioned
rest of A DIVE

explanation.surface: A Frenchman remarks on an extra that turned up in a sleazy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An additive is something added to supplement food or fuel, such as a preservative.

clue.text: Urge that's current to divide two parties

indicators.note: something that divides two things comes between them

parts.note: the Liberals, a political party
I is the symbol for electric current
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A political movement whose present aim is to split two parties apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The two parties are of different kinds: one political, one a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire or drive, an instinctive urge.

clue.text: Transformation in earthy girl on vacation showing sluggishness

indicators.note: a transformation changes the form, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside letters leave and only the ends stay

parts.note: first and last letters of girl

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth young woman away on holiday changes, becoming listless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a lack of energy and enthusiasm, the same as sluggishness.

clue.text: Horseman in black period, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: A rider appears in the dark hours, so the story goes.
